core/directional_dpi.c:501-509 clamps out_int to +/-32767, then sets new_rem = total_q16 - out_int*65536 and stores it via clamp_rem_i32, which caps at +/-2147418112 (lines 472-480), under the comment 'Carry any excess beyond report clamp in remainder instead of dropping it'. ddpi_engine_set_profile (lines 327-336) calls ddpi_engine_reset_remainders, which zeroes rem_x/y and dir_x/y, only when ddpi_profile_is_identity() is true. I copied the .c and .h files to /tmp/claude-1000/-home-lloen-src-kineforge/95815f0b-46c2-4973-91bb-aaae9ed96bbc/scratchpad/verify/odd/harness.c and built them with gcc -std=c11 -Wall -Wextra. Feeding dx=30000 into a 16x profile (4x multipliers, 4x gain) gave out=32767 with rem_x=2147418112, which is exactly 32767 counts. The next two dx=1 calls returned 32767 and then 32, so the remainder was drained. A non-identity set_profile left rem at 2147418112, and setting a disabled (identity) profile reset it to 0. One limit: anything beyond one extra report (32767 counts) is still lost when the remainder saturates. In the run above about 414k of the 480k counts were dropped. 'Identity' also covers disabled and calibration-bypass profiles. An ONLY_AT_BASE_DPI mismatch does not trigger the reset.

calibration/cli.ts:79-80 sets p.reserved = opts.windowCounts ?? Math.min(DDPI_MAX_WINDOW_COUNTS, Math.max(1, Math.round(p.baseDpi / 50.8))), and DDPI_MAX_WINDOW_COUNTS = 128 (integrations/openmouse/src/directional-dpi.ts:42). The Math.max(1, ...) floor never matters, because clampDpi keeps baseDpi >= 50. p.baseDpi is the recommended sensor CPI: the playing DPI, or the raised DPI for cpi-headroom. web/calibrate.html:456-460 runs try { await canvas.requestPointerLock({ unadjustedMovement: true }) } catch { canvas.requestPointerLock(); }. MDN says unadjustedMovement defaults to false and that setting it to true 'will disable mouse acceleration'. So the plain fallback is OS-accelerated. Browsers whose requestPointerLock returns no promise never reach the catch and silently get an accelerated lock.

results.evidence: Directive 2009/24/EC, OJ L 111/16. Art. 5(3): "The person having a right to use a copy of a computer program shall be entitled ... to observe, study or test the functioning of the program". results.corrected_statement: The opfs-sahpool VFS does not need COOP/COEP headers and works only in Worker threads. Concurrency is limited rather than absent. It does not support several simultaneous connections to the same database, with two exceptions: connections within the same thread (versions before 3.54 have a locking bug that can corrupt the database in that case), and connections coordinated by client code through PoolUtil.pauseVfs() and unpauseVfs(), available since 3.50. Only one instance of the VFS per origin and directory can be installed at a time, so a second tab fails to install it.
results.evidence: In the sqlite.org persistence.md section on opfs-sahpool, the listed advantages include "Does not require COOP/COEP HTTP headers (and associated restrictions)". The listed disadvantages include no multiple simultaneous connections to the same database, except within the same thread or with explicit help from client code. The page also says installation fails when the OPFS APIs are missing, because "They are only available in Worker threads, not the main UI thread". It describes pauseVfs() and unpauseVfs() as a way to hand the files to another tab or Worker.

glam-0.34.3 crate (sse2.rs and neon.rs are identical to 0.34.0). Vec4 and Quat dot: sse2.rs dot4_into_m128 says "keeping the (x + z) + (y + w) grouping". neon.rs dot4 uses vaddvq_f32, which adds in pairs as (x+y)+(z+w). f32/scalar/vec4.rs:244 sums left to right, ((x+y)+z)+w. Vec3A dot is the same everywhere: SSE2 dot3_in_x does _mm_add_ss(x+y, z), f32/neon/vec3a.rs:255 uses the plain scalar expression ("this was faster than intrinsics"), and scalar is (x+y)+z. No dot function uses FMA. Under cfg(target_feature="fma"), m128_mul_add/m128_neg_mul_sub (sse2.rs:133-160) are used by Vec3A::cross, Quat mul, slerp, lerp_monotonic, mul_add and sin_cos. NEON calls vfmaq_f32 always, with no feature gate (quat.rs:707/833, vec4.rs:1045/1155). src/f64/ contains no arch:: or SIMD code, and DVec3::dot and DQuat::dot are plain scalar.
results.corrected_statement: In glam 0.34.x, the summation order differs by backend only for 4-wide dot products (Vec4, Quat): SSE2 sums (x+z)+(y+w), NEON (x+y)+(z+w), and scalar ((x+y)+z)+w. Vec3A dot sums (x+y)+z on SSE2, NEON and scalar alike. No dot product uses FMA. The SSE2 backend uses FMA only when target_feature="fma" is enabled, in cross, Quat mul, slerp, lerp_monotonic, mul_add and sin/cos. The NEON backend uses vfmaq unconditionally in Quat mul, slerp, lerp_monotonic and mul_add. The f64 types (DVec*, DQuat, DMat*) have only a scalar implementation.

results.evidence: In std library/std/src/num/f32.rs (stable), sin, cos, atan2, powf, exp, ln (and tan, hypot, powi) each carry the note: "The precision of this function is non-deterministic. This means it varies by platform, Rust version, and can even differ within the same execution". sqrt and mul_add say the result "is guaranteed to be the rounded infinite-precision result" and name the IEEE 754 operation (squareRoot / fusedMultiplyAdd). RFC 3514 covers +, -, *, /, %, abs, copysign, mul_add, sqrt and casts, which "produce results that exactly match IEEE 754-2008". Exceptions: NaN bit patterns, and known non-conforming targets such as i586/x87.
results.corrected_statement: Confirmed. One caveat: RFC 3514's exact-IEEE guarantee excludes NaN sign and payload bits, which are non-deterministic, and is knowingly violated on 32-bit x86 without SSE2 (x87 excess precision, tracking issue #114479).

results.evidence: RFC 3514 makes * and + exactly IEEE, and its rationale says this "precludes many transformations, such as turning a*b + c into FMA". It adds that such transformations require "explicit opt-in". rustc's PassWrapper.cpp (main) never sets AllowFPOpFusion, so LLVM keeps its default FPOpFusion::Standard, which allows "fusion of 'blessed' ops (currently just fmuladd)" (TargetOptions.h, llvmorg-20.1.0). rustc emits fast-math or contract flags only for the explicit fadd_fast and *_algebraic intrinsics (rustc_codegen_llvm builder.rs:611-620). The relaxed fmuladd semantics are exposed only as explicit opt-in methods (mul_add_relaxed, PR #151793, merged). The NVPTX backend fuses only when -nvptx-fma-level is passed, Fast fusion is set, or unsafe-fp-math is on.
results.corrected_statement: Confirmed for the default LLVM backend. Contraction happens only on explicit opt-in: f32::mul_add, mul_add_relaxed, the algebraic_* methods, or user-passed -C llvm-args such as -fp-contract=fast or -nvptx-fma-level. Separately, i586 (x87) targets do not round a*b+c to IEEE results because of excess precision; this is not FMA fusion.

results.evidence: Rand book crate-reprod.md declares rand::rngs::SmallRng and rand::rngs::StdRng "non-portable", meaning each "opts out of all reproducibility guarantees". rand CHANGELOG 0.9.0 lists: Uniform now uses Canon's and Lemire's methods "(breaks value stability; #1287)"; "New, faster algorithms for SliceRandom::shuffle and partial_shuffle (#1272)"; and new algorithms for IteratorRandom::choose (#1268). rand 0.10.0 (2026-02-08): "The dependency on rand_chacha has been replaced with a dependency on chacha20", and StdRng output remains the same. The current release is 0.10.3.
results.corrected_statement: Confirmed. Two details: the book's non-portable-items policy applies from rand 0.10 (up to 0.9, non-portable items could not change values in patch releases), and the 0.10 switch to chacha20 kept StdRng output unchanged.

results.evidence: libm 0.2.16 (2026-01-24, the latest) describes itself as "libm in pure Rust". 52 source files carry "origin: FreeBSD" headers inherited from musl, and cbrt is ported from CORE-MATH. src/math/arch/mod.rs overrides only exactly-rounded ops on the three targets. x86 with SSE2: sqrt, sqrtf, fma, fmaf (fma picks hardware or software at runtime, both exact). aarch64: fma, rint, sqrt. wasm32: ceil, fabs, floor, rint, sqrt, trunc, and only with the unstable-intrinsics cfg. The only transcendental overrides are x87 exp/exp2/exp10 on x86 without SSE. Neither the README nor the docs states a cross-platform identical-results guarantee. NaNs are produced arithmetically, e.g. log.rs:88 `(x - x) / 0.0` and pow.rs:217 `(x - x) / (x - x)`, so per RFC 3514 their bit patterns are hardware-dependent (x86 default NaN has the sign bit set; ARM and wasm do not).
results.corrected_statement: libm 0.2.16 is a pure-Rust libm, mostly ported from musl/FreeBSD msun, with some newer code such as CORE-MATH cbrt and generic rewrites. On x86_64, aarch64 and wasm32 it overrides only exactly-rounded ops (sqrt, fma, rint, and on wasm32 with unstable intrinsics also floor, ceil, trunc and fabs), and its transcendental code paths are the same on all three. Because Rust guarantees IEEE basic ops with no contraction, non-NaN results should therefore be bit-identical. This follows from reading the source; libm documents no such guarantee. NaN sign and payload bits can differ by architecture. On i586 (x86 without SSE), x87 overrides exist for exp, exp2 and exp10.
